course_name_original: Fundamentos De Ciencia De Los Materiales Ii
prerequisites: Must have completed "Fundamentals of Materials Science I"

learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and skills for the application of materials engineering.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is typically at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional manner and possess the competencies typically demonstrated by developing and defending arguments and solving problems within their field of study.
Students have the ability to gather and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include reflection on relevant social, scientific, or ethical issues.
Students have developed the learning skills necessary to undertake further studies with a high degree of autonomy.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for performing measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to analyze and assess the social and environmental impact of technical solutions.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.

syllabus_topics: Topic 1. Non-ferrous alloys of industrial interest. Treatments, characteristics, and applications
Topic 2. Polymeric materials of industrial interest
Topic 3. Ceramic materials of industrial interest
Topic 4. Composite materials of industrial interest
Topic 5. In-service behavior and degradation of materials
teaching_methods: Reading guidelines available in the virtual course
Study of topics through basic bibliography and complementary material
Individual work: analytical reading of each topic, elaboration of outlines, completion of learning activities
Interactive application for materials selection (Granta Edupack Introductory)
assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated from a Continuous Assessment Test (PEC, up to 20% for EC students), a Compulsory Assignment (up to 10% for all students), and a Face-to-face Exam (up to 70% for EC students, up to 90% for non-EC students). To pass, students must achieve a minimum of 3 points in the exam's test section, complete the compulsory assignment, and obtain an overall score of at least 5 points. In the test section, correct answers add 0.7 points, while incorrect answers subtract 0.35 points. PEC and Compulsory Assignment scores are maintained for the September resit period.
